programme: GATA3 and STAT6 form the canonical Th2/type-2 polarization axis (GATA3 as master driver of IL4/IL5/IL13-centered transcription, STAT6 as the IL-4/IL-13 receptor-activated partner sharing the same target genes), with HDAC1 acting as the chromatin corepressor that sets the transcriptional output of this same locus set (via NuRD/CoREST-type repression), and PIAS2, a SUMO E3 ligase of the STAT-inhibitory PIAS family, providing negative feedback on the same signaling axis.
role_in_a: In COVID-19, GATA3/STAT6-driven Th2 skewing of T-cell responses is documented directly (IL-4+ memory T cells after booster vaccination, PMID 40884220; broader review of GATA3 signaling in disease, PMID 39768217), while HDAC1 is an independently validated host factor: its inhibition increases SARS-CoV-2 replication in lung cells (PMID 38162580) and it is an active dual-inhibitor drug target alongside AAK1 (PMID 39581172), with a further link to genetic susceptibility of severity (PMID 42650152). Together these place a Th2-polarization/chromatin-repression axis in blood immune responses to SARS-CoV-2.
role_in_b: Nothing in the retrieved record places GATA3, STAT6, HDAC1, or PIAS2 in fibromyalgia specifically — the fibromyalgia-side hits for these factors were off-topic (schizophrenia, dental disorders) or absent. Outside this record, fibromyalgia has been proposed in places to involve a mild Th2-leaning cytokine shift and low-grade neuroinflammation in blood, but that is a general and contested strand of the field, not evidence tied to these particular factors.
shared_axis: If real, the shared axis would be that both a viral infection (COVID-19) and a chronic pain/neuroimmune condition (fibromyalgia) can engage the same blood-resident Th2 transcriptional module and its epigenetic brake, from different upstream triggers (antiviral T-cell skewing vs. stress/pain-driven immune dysregulation), producing convergent bulk-blood regulon signatures without a shared causal driver.
reasoning: The four carrying factors form a real, nameable module (a Th2 master pair plus its known corepressor and STAT-feedback regulator), and GATA3/HDAC1 are independently documented in COVID-19, so the module is not invented from noise. But no paper here or established clinical view ties this axis to fibromyalgia, and FM is not conventionally treated as a Th2-polarized disease, so the pairing is unexpected rather than a known or obviously-inferable fact. Strength is moderate rather than strong because only two of the four carrying factors (GATA3, HDAC1) have concrete disease-specific literature, and it all sits on the COVID-19 side only.
support: PMID 39768217 (GATA3 signaling mechanisms and disease relevance, COVID-19 context); PMID 40884220 (IL-4+ memory T cells in SARS-CoV-2 booster vaccination — direct GATA3/Th2-axis evidence in COVID-19); PMID 38768914 (GATA3-adjacent inhibitor screen in a COVID-19-relevant immune target panel, weaker relevance); PMID 38162580 (HDAC1-3 inhibition increases SARS-CoV-2 replication in lung cells); PMID 39581172 (AAK1/HDAC dual inhibitors developed against SARS-CoV-2); PMID 42650152 (whole-exome study of COVID-19 severity susceptibility genes, including HDAC1). No PMID above supports any of these four factors in fibromyalgia.
how_to_falsify: Score matched whole-blood or PBMC transcriptomes from COVID-19 and fibromyalgia cohorts for coordinated activity of the GATA3/STAT6 target set (IL4, IL5, IL13, IFNG and shared neighbors) and for HDAC1 occupancy/repression at those same loci; if fibromyalgia samples show no coordinated shift in this regulon relative to controls (or no PIAS2-associated feedback signature) while COVID-19 samples do, the claimed shared programme is false and the concordance is more likely an artifact of the network-inference pipeline or of generic blood cell-composition differences between cohorts.
caveats: Both diseases are sampled in blood, and the 16/16 concordance spans only 2 independent cohort pairs, so the perfect recurrence reflects agreement within a small number of underlying cohorts rather than broad independent replication. The tissue-generic exclusion list removed several bona fide immune/chromatin regulators (NFATC1, FOS, EZH2, ETS1/ETS2, MEF2C, TWIST1, RORA, LITAF, ID3, FOXO3, and single-view E2F3/TAL1) that might otherwise have anchored a more conventional immune-activation story — their absence here is due to that filter, not evidence against immune involvement. Most of the 12 listed concordant factors (HOXA13, DMTF1, PITX1, AIP, NR2C2, TBP, SMARCA1, ZFP64) do not fit into the Th2/HDAC1/PIAS2 account and are left unexplained; this account covers only 4 of the 12 factors given.
